clue.text: Priest about to back one making sign of cross

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole assembled piece in the opposite direction
about means surrounding, so the priest's title goes round the next word

parts.note: REV is the short form of Reverend, a title for a priest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman turning round to bless someone who crosses themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TO inside REV to make RETOV, and 'back' turns all of it round. The 'sign of cross' is the X put on a ballot paper, not a religious gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone casting a ballot marks a cross beside a candidate, so an elector is one making that sign.

clue.text: Blue badge learner lost — may it be on motorcycle?

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed

indicators.note: lost suggests letters wandering astray, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gloomy biker who has lost the learner badge from the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges BADGE plus L into DLEBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Panniers or pouches hung at the side of a motorbike or horse are called by this name.

clue.text: Throw pickle around cold stew

parts.note: to lob is to throw in a high arc

indicators.note: around means the pickling word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: to souse is to pickle in brine or vinegar
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone tossing pickles into a cold pot of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C inside SOUSE to make SCOUSE. Lobscouse is a sailors' stew, the origin of 'Scouse' for Liverpudlians.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobscouse is a meat and vegetable stew eaten by sailors and in Liverpool.

clue.text: Guardian spirit, not a single kind

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the following letter

parts.note: a genius in Roman belief was a guardian spirit of a person or place
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A protective spirit described as being of no single type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes the I from GENIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a class or sort grouping related species.

clue.text: Drunk at back of car, as some wine may be

indicators.note: at back of puts the word for drunk after the car word

parts.note: an estate is a British car with a large load space at the rear
bottled is British slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk sprawled in the back of a car, like a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine bottled at the vineyard where it was made is labelled with this term.

clue.text: At front of demo, curious? Beat it!

indicators.note: at front of picks the opening letter of the word demo

parts.note: rum is British informal for odd or curious

explanation.surface: A nosy onlooker at the head of a protest march being told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it!' reads as 'go away', but 'it' only links: to drum is to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To drum is to beat repeatedly, as with sticks or fingers.

clue.text: An irritatingly small performance?

parts.note: a show put on by tiny biting insects, which are both small and irritating

explanation.surface: A complaint about a show that was annoyingly short.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novelty sideshow in which trained insects supposedly perform tricks.

clue.text: Final outcome of Times operation?

parts.note: the result of multiplying numbers, read as the last result of any process

explanation.surface: Asking how a newspaper's project turned out in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means multiplication, whose result is a product.
explanation.definitionFit: The finished item or final result of a process is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Hurray for an exam!

definitions.meaning: a ... is an oral examination, short for ... voce

explanation.surface: Cheering for a test.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exclamation of acclaim and a spoken university examination.

clue.text: Tune librarian reviewed, a patriotic one

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking over again and reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A librarian reviewing a patriotic song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges TUNE and LIBRARIAN together; 'one' in the definition stands for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This stirring British song is a famous patriotic anthem.

clue.text: Crashing to earth as wings fail, having no supplements

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outermost letters, and they drop away

parts.note: falling describes something crashing down

explanation.surface: A plane coming down as its wings give out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings fail' removes the outer F and G of FALLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclusive price covers everything, so there are no extras to pay.

clue.text: Ineffective name adopted by plain resort

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the plain word holds the other pieces

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
a dud is something that fails to work

explanation.surface: A useless name taken on by a dull seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' puts DUDN inside LLANO. Llandudno is a seaside resort in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a well-known Victorian seaside holiday town on the Welsh coast.

clue.text: Hurt after exercise, I am first to be disparaged

indicators.note: after places the word for hurt behind the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
PE is physical education, school exercise
ached means hurt

explanation.surface: Someone sore after a workout complaining of being belittled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts IM at the front, before PE and ACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impeached is to have one's honour or credibility called into question.

clue.text: City's new half back

indicators.note: back means the word for half is read in reverse

parts.note: semi is a prefix and word meaning half

explanation.surface: A football club's new half-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEMI into IMES. Half-back is a football position, which sets up the misdirection. NIMES is a city in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimes is a city in southern France famous for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Cunningly evaded dual basis for taxation

indicators.note: cunningly suggests craftily rearranged, signalling the letters move about

explanation.surface: Someone cleverly dodging two taxes at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' rearranges EVADED and DUAL. VAT is the UK's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Value added tax is levied on the increase in worth at each stage of production.

clue.text: Rather fat, dropping by for bath

indicators.note: dropping means leaving out the following word

parts.note: tubby means rather fat

explanation.surface: A plump person losing weight in the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes BY from TUBBY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is an informal word for a bathtub.

clue.text: Go through park with unmarried couple

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a park

indicators.note: un means without, and M is the abbreviation for married, so that letter goes

parts.note: an item is a romantic couple

explanation.surface: Going through the park with a pair of cohabiting lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmarried' removes M (married) from ITEM, leaving ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to go through something aloud from memory.

clue.text: Argued young bird looked injured

parts.note: a squab is a young pigeon
someone who bled showed a wound

explanation.surface: A fledgling looked hurt after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To squabble is to quarrel noisily over something trivial, so argued fits the past tense.

clue.text: Once you serve, say, rabbit stew, half's disappearing

parts.note: a doe is a female rabbit

indicators.note: half of the word stew vanishes, so only its front half remains

explanation.surface: Cooking a rabbit stew and serving it while half of it vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic form: 'thou doest' was old English for 'you do', and serve is an example of doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doest is the archaic second person singular of do, as in serving.

clue.text: Call set up to introduce a subsidy for action

indicators.note: to introduce means bringing a letter into the middle of the reversed pair
in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: to dial is to call by phone
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A phone call arranged to bring in funding for an action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIAL and GEL into LEGLAID, and 'to introduce' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Public money paying for legal representation in court is subsidy for a lawsuit.

clue.text: Church service, one taking place to support monk

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath

parts.note: Saint Benedict founded the Benedictine order of monks
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means happening, as in the show is on

explanation.surface: An ordained man stepping in to back up a monk at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts I and ON beneath BENEDICT in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A benediction is a blessing, and also a short devotional church service.

clue.text: Gallon remains surplus

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A gallon of leftovers is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: GASH is British naval slang for spare or extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang gash means spare or superfluous, so excess matter.

clue.text: From lunch, depart drunk — that's shockingly unexpected

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leaving lunch drunk comes as an unpleasant surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters of LUNCH and DEPART.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden alarming event is figuratively a bolt from the blue, like a loud boom of thunder.

clue.text: Struggling at lacrosse, they run up and down

indicators.note: struggling suggests things going awry, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Players having a hard time at lacrosse, running up and down the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges AT LACROSSE. The surface suggests players running up and down a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases carry people upward and downward between floors.

clue.text: Man, shrewd one, lacking charm

parts.note: arch means knowing or sly
I is the Roman numeral for one
bald means plain and unadorned, with no grace

explanation.surface: A cunning fellow with no charm at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Archibald is a man's first name, so it fits a man as an example.

clue.text: Voices raised around long, thin island

indicators.note: around means the reversed word surrounds the next piece
in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: airs are tunes or melodies, voiced songs
lank means long and thin

explanation.surface: Singers lifting their voices round a tall skinny figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns AIRS into SRIA, and 'around' puts LANK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation off the southern tip of India.

clue.text: What indulgence!

definitions.meaning: what? is a request to repeat something, said politely another way
an indulgence was a church remission of punishment for sin

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone's excess.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a polite request to repeat and a remission of sins.

clue.text: Be forcibly expelled as ringer, leaving a large church

indicators.note: leaving means dropping the next letter

parts.note: a bell is something that rings
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer kicked out of a big church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes one L from BELL, giving BEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke or flame belching from a chimney is forced out violently.

clue.text: Overthrowing religion has not succeeded in country

indicators.note: has not means the following letter is missing
overthrowing means turning upside down, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: Islam is a world religion
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A coup against a faith that failed in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrowing' turns ISLAM into MALSI, and 'has not' removes the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Clipping small coin is stupid

indicators.note: clipping means trimming the last letter off

parts.note: a dime is a small US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Shaving metal from a little coin is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipping' removes the final E of DIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim is an informal word for slow-witted.
